text:
Kiefer Sherwood is the rare player whose best stat is the one nobody else wants: 113 hits in 22 games, more than five a night, from a forward who set the NHL's single-season hits record in Vancouver two years ago. He's also the Sharks' most quotable player, having called out the Kings for "disrespectful" antics during a 6-2 loss, and the team's mic'd-up video of him has been a hit of its own.

The scoring has gone missing. After 23 goals last season, he has two this year on 3.7 expected, and he's pointless in six straight. Our form check says the chances have thinned out over that stretch too, so this isn't only bad luck. San Jose takes 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, about the same as without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, 79th among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 52% of his shots come off the rush. On a team that spends a lot of time defending, that's the part to watch: when the Sharks start getting out in transition, Sherwood's goals should follow.
